guard: a smoke broker owned through the helper dies when its suite is SIGNALLED, not only when the suite returns
why: ONE MUTATION, AND IT REMOVES OWNERSHIP, NOT A HOOK. Two earlier fixtures here came back UNGRADABLE:
one disabled the SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers, one disabled the `exit` handler, and the suite
stayed 14/14 through both. Both verdicts were correct and the diagnosis was mine to find.
WHAT THOSE TWO NON-KILLS ESTABLISHED, which no single run could have. The hooks are INDEPENDENTLY
SUFFICIENT under `tsx`. If a signal listener exists, tsx delivers the signal and the handler reaps.
If none exists, tsx converts the signal into an ordinary exit and the `exit` handler reaps: measured
directly, a fixture registering only `process.on("exit")`, sent SIGTERM at its own pid, printed
`EXIT HANDLER RAN code=143`. So disabling either one alone leaves the other doing the work, and a
mutation on either hook can only ever be UNGRADABLE. The property under test is that the broker is
OWNED; which hook carries it out is an implementation detail of the runner.
THE SUITE'S POSITIVE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THE KILL MEAN SOMETHING. Cell 1 runs the identical
fixture WITHOUT ownership and asserts the broker SURVIVES, so the suite is known to be able to see a
leak. This mutation makes every cell take the control's path, so the control MUST stay green while
the owned cells flip. A mutation that reddened the control too would be measuring the ambient
behaviour rather than the helper.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE, and the suite prints it rather than leaving it to be assumed. The signal
handlers are UNOBSERVED under `tsx`: they are kept for a runner that does not intercept, where a
default-disposition signal would skip `exit` entirely, and no cell here exercises that runner.
SIGKILL is uncatchable under either, which cell 5 asserts as a fact rather than omitting. And the
helper only ever fires if the signal REACHES the suite process, which is two node processes below
`pnpm`; a supervisor that kills the top pid alone never signals it.
